logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HFmrEF (LVEF 41%-49%), SGLT2 inhibitors can be beneficial in decreasing HF hospitalizations and cardiovascular mortality. Based on EMPEROR-Preserved trial data showing 21% reduction in composite of HF hospitalization or cardiovascular death.

source_text: In patients with HFmrEF, SGLT2i can be beneficial in decreasing HF hospitalizations and cardiovascular mortality. (COR 2a, LOE B-R)

logic_node.action: Consider evidence-based beta blockers for HFmrEF
logic_node.action_detail: Among patients with current or previous symptomatic HFmrEF (LVEF 41%-49%), use of evidence-based beta blockers for HFrEF may be considered to reduce the risk of HF hospitalization and cardiovascular mortality, particularly among patients with LVEF on the lower end of this spectrum.

source_text: Among patients with current or previous symptomatic HFmrEF (LVEF, 41%-49%), use of evidence-based beta blockers for HFrEF... may be considered to reduce the risk of HF hospitalization and cardiovascular mortality.

logic_node.action_detail: Among patients with current or previous symptomatic HFmrEF (LVEF 41%-49%), use of ARNi (sacubitril/valsartan) may be considered to reduce the risk of HF hospitalization and cardiovascular mortality, particularly among patients with LVEF on the lower end of this spectrum. PARAGON-HF subgroup analysis for LVEF 45%-57% suggested benefit of sacubitril-valsartan versus valsartan alone.

source_text: Among patients with current or previous symptomatic HFmrEF (LVEF, 41%-49%), use of... ARNi... may be considered to reduce the risk of HF hospitalization and cardiovascular mortality.

logic_node.action: Consider ACE inhibitor or ARB for HFmrEF
logic_node.action_detail: Among patients with current or previous symptomatic HFmrEF (LVEF 41%-49%), use of ACEi or ARB may be considered to reduce the risk of HF hospitalization and cardiovascular mortality, particularly among patients with LVEF on the lower end of this spectrum. CHARM trials subgroup showed candesartan reduced risk of cardiovascular death and HF hospitalization in LVEF 41%-49%.

source_text: Among patients with current or previous symptomatic HFmrEF (LVEF, 41%-49%), use of... ACEi, or ARB... may be considered to reduce the risk of HF hospitalization and cardiovascular mortality.

logic_node.action_detail: Among patients with current or previous symptomatic HFmrEF (LVEF 41%-49%), use of MRAs (e.g., spironolactone) may be considered to reduce the risk of HF hospitalization and cardiovascular mortality. Spironolactone is preferred among HFmrEF patients with poorly controlled hypertension. TOPCAT subgroup (LVEF 44%-49%) showed spironolactone reduced composite of CV death, HF hospitalization, or resuscitated sudden death.

source_text: Among patients with current or previous symptomatic HFmrEF (LVEF, 41%-49%), use of... MRAs may be considered to reduce the risk of HF hospitalization and cardiovascular mortality.

logic_node.action: Repeat LVEF evaluation to determine disease trajectory
logic_node.action_detail: Patients with HFmrEF should have repeat evaluation of LVEF to determine the trajectory of their disease process and should undergo testing as clinically indicated to diagnose conditions warranting disease-specific therapy (e.g., CAD, sarcoidosis, amyloidosis).

source_text: Patients with HFmrEF should have repeat evaluation of LVEF to determine the trajectory of their disease process and should undergo testing as clinically indicated to diagnose conditions warranting disease-specific therapy.

logic_node.action: Continue GDMT to prevent HF relapse
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HFimpEF (previously HFrEF with improved LVEF) after treatment, GDMT should be continued to prevent relapse of HF and LV dysfunction, even in patients who may become asymptomatic. Withdrawal of HF medications resulted in relapse of cardiomyopathy and HF in 40% of patients within 6 months in an open-label RCT.

source_text: In patients with HFimpEF after treatment, GDMT should be continued to prevent relapse of HF and LV dysfunction, even in patients who may become asymptomatic. (COR 1, LOE B-R)
